GRAPH STRUCTURED DATA MINING

New Graph Neural Network Architectures (☞ Slide)
Due to the complex structures and large scales, it is hard to make predictions directly, thus the existing approaches turn to compress the meticulous structures into only two nodes with one edge, which may bring in noise and suffer from data sparsity. We call this the early summarization issue and propose Heterogeneous INteract and aggreGatE (GraphHINGE) to capture and aggregate the interactive patterns between each pair of nodes through their structured neighborhoods. [KDD 2020] [TOIS 2021] [🏆 AWS Machine Learning Research Project Award] In order to bridge between symbolic semantics and subgraph topology, we propose ANalogy subGraph Embedding Learning (GraphANGEL) to make prediction of each node pair based on the subgraphs containing the pair, as well as other (analogy) subgraphs with the same graph patterns. [ICLR 2022a] These researches are supported by Deep Graph Library Team.
Simple Enhancements on Graph Neural Networks for Node and Edge Predictions (☞ Slide)
Graph neural networks and label propagation represent two interrelated modeling strategies designed to exploit graph structure. We propose a Label Trick to accommodate the parallel use of features and labels, which uses a randomly-selected portion of the training labels as model inputs, concatenated with the original node features for making predictions on the remaining labels. [DLG-KDD 2021] [🏆 Best Paper Award] It is foundational to many of the top-ranking submissions on the Open Graph Benchmark leaderboard. We further theoretically show that under certain simplifying assumptions, the stochastic label trick can be reduced to an interpretable, deterministic training objective. [ICLR 2022b] These researches are supported by Deep Graph Library Team.
Graph Structure Enhancements for Learning and Planning (☞ Slide)
Besides the graph data in the real-world scenarioes, we demonstrate that the latent graph structures such as state-transition graphs are also benefitical to learning algorithms. In this regard, we propose Graph Enhanced Goal Oriented Reinforcement Learning (G2RL) for effective exploration and efficient training based on learning and planning on state-transition graphs. [ICLR 2022c]

SEQUENCE STRUCTURED DATA MINING

New Sequential Neural Network Architectures (☞ Slide)
Implicit feedback (e.g., user clicks) is an important source of data for modern search engines. While heavily biased, it is cheap to collect and particularly useful for user-centric retrieval applications. To develop an unbiased ranker with biased feedback, we propose Deep Recurrent Survival Ranking (DRSR) that incorporates survival analysis techniques with recurrent neural network to derive user feedbacks at each position. [SIGIR 2020a] This research is supported by Alibaba Innovative Research Program. As users’ demands are not only conditioned by their profile but also by their recent browsing behaviors as well as periodical purchases made some time ago, we propose Search-based Time-Aware Recommendation (STARec) which captures the evolving demands of users over time through a unified search-based time-aware model. This research is supported by China Merchants Bank, and has been successfully deployed at China Merchants Bank App. [WWW 2022a] [🔌 Real-world Deployment]
Applications of Sequential Models on E-Commerce (☞ Slide)
With the prevalence of live broadcast business nowadays, live broadcast recommendation, is widely used in many mobile e-commerce Apps. We propose TWo-side Interactive NetworkS (TWINS) to fully mine the interactive patterns of both static and dynamic information on user and anchor sides. [WWW 2022b] This research is supported by Alibaba Innovative Research Program, and has been successfully deployed at Taobao Live App. [🔌 Real-world Deployment]

UNSTRUCTURED DATA MINING

Learning and Planning on Unstructured Data (☞ Slide)
In a general view, there are two major decision-making tasks for such ride-hailing platforms, namely order dispatching and fleet management. Most of the previous work deals with either order dispatching or fleet management without regarding the high correlation of these two tasks. We propose CoRide to jointly model order dispatching and fleet management with hierarchical reinforcement learning. This research is supported by DiDi Athena Joint Talent Program. [CIKM 2019a] [🏆 Gaia Young Scholar Outstanding Project Award] As users’ demands are not only conditioned by their profile but also by their previous browsing behaviors, we propose User Behavior Retrieval (UBR) to incorporate users' related historical records to make predictions. [SIGIR 2020b]

GAME

Personal Computer Game (☞ Code)
Be a Hero. Let's go through this level game on Windows. My team (as the Team Leader, cooperated with Zhuang Guan and Chufeng Tan) build an operational game in C++ without any engine (over 10,000 lines).
Website Game (☞ Website)
Inspired by Get MIT, we develop 2048 game Here. Use your arrow keys to move the tiles. When two tiles with the same college touch, they merge into one! NOTE: The order of colleges is not intended to be a ranking, but a rough north-to-south geographical path to SJTU.
